title: Finite coefficients on the étale site
statement:
Fix a prime $p$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, a field $k_0$ with $q$ elements and an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, as in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Put $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on their small etale sites in the derived categories of constant-coefficient module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, where $D^b_c$ means bounded cohomology with each cohomology sheaf constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Require finite Tor amplitude for $L$: there exist integers $u\leq v$ such that for every sheaf $M$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, placed in degree zero, $\mathcal H^i(L\otimes^L_\Lambda M)=0$ for $i\notin[u,v]$. Use the ordinary etale derived tensor product [def-kun-derived-tensor] and the exact constant-coefficient inverse image $Lf^*=f^{-1}$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $Rf_!$ be the ordinary etale compact-support direct image, represented by $Rr_*j_!$ for a compactification $f=rj$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Use the projection notation of [def-sf-pf]: let $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ denote the canonical compact-support projection transformation on these etale categories appearing in [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], of type

$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow Rf_!\bigl(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L\bigr).
$$

Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism in $D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, naturally in $K$ and $L$.

proof.text: Apply the etale assertion of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] with $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and with precisely the given $f,K,L$. Its hypotheses are the fixed finite-field datum, separated finite-type $f$ between finite-type $k$-schemes, bounded constructible $K,L$ on the small etale sites, and finite Tor amplitude for $L$ with the tensor-vanishing definition on that site; all have been imposed here. Its displayed map is exactly the etale compact-support projection transformation denoted $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ in the statement. The lemma asserts that this map is an isomorphism and is natural in both variables. Only its etale assertion is used; no pro-etale comparison or abstract six-functor axiom is needed.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, let
$f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, and let $K$ and $L$ be bounded
constructible complexes on the étale sites with $L$ of finite Tor
amplitude. Then $\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}$ is an isomorphism, natural in
$K$ and $L$ ([lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]).

proof.text:
The projection transformation used below is [def-sf-pf], and the
finite compact-support case is
[lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula].
Step 1: split off a compactification $f=\bar f\circ j$; then
$Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ and the projection transformation is the composite of
the direct-image projection map for $\bar f$ with the identification
$j_!K\otimes^L\bar f^*L\cong j_!(K\otimes^Lf^*L)$, which is checked on
étale stalks (on the open $X$ both sides have stalk
$K_{\bar x}\otimes L_{\bar x}$, and off $X$ both are zero). Step 2: for a
geometric point $\bar y\to Y$ with fibre $X_{\bar y}$, compact-support base
change identifies the stalk of the projection map with
$R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y})\otimes^L P\to R\Gamma_c(X_{\bar y},K^{\mathrm{fib}}_{\bar y}\otimes^L\underline P)$,
where $P=L_{\bar y}$ and $\underline P$ is the pullback of the complex of
$A_{E,n}$-modules $P$. Step 3: the fibrewise map is an isomorphism for
every $P$: choosing a bounded complex of finite free modules representing
$P$, both sides are exact functors of $P$ agreeing on $P=A_{E,n}$ (the unit
identification), and the class of $P$ for which the map is an isomorphism
is closed under finite sums, shifts, cones and direct summands. Step 4:
all geometric stalks of the cone vanish, and geometric stalks are
conservative on the étale site, so the cone is zero.
